### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.comment

### Question

Hello,

I develop websites using the Svelte framework and started to use `mini.comment` recently. Previously I was using `tomtom/tcomment_vim`.

I have realised that the comments don't seem to work in the `.svelte` files. I assume this is possibly because these files have parts in JS, parts in HTML, parts in CSS/SCSS, etc. Although I thought tree sitter was taking care of informing plugins of the subtypes inside a file, but I may be wrong. With `tcomment` there were a few quirks but it was working in the grand scheme of things.

When I do try, my cursor jumps to the first non-blank char of the current line, and the following message is printed :

```
(mini.comment) Option 'commentstring' is empty.
``` 

Am I missing something in the settings that would make it work? or is it simply something not implemented yet?

comment_data.body:
### About

You probably don't even need `mini.comment`, since commenting is already built into Neovim, with `mini.comment` serving as the reference implementation. You can probably guess who actually brought it into the core.

Treesitter helps to determine the appropriate `commentstring` for the cursor position, bypassing `vim.bo.commentstring`. Basically, you need to configure treesitter parsers for `svelte` and its injected languages, such as `javascript` and `css`.

From [:h commenting](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/28d641b5607025c34153e11272fbd270ac673f85/runtime/doc/various.txt#L637-L641):

> ```help
> If the filetype of the buffer is associated with a language for which a
> |treesitter| parser is installed, then |vim.filetype.get_option()| is called
> to look up the value of 'commentstring' corresponding to the cursor position.
> (This can be different from the buffer's 'commentstring' in case of
> |treesitter-language-injections|.)
> ```

### Debug

That said, are you sure the treesitter parsers are installed correctly?

Run:

```vim
:InspectTree
I
```

It should **not** print:

```text
Failed to create TSTreeView for buffer 1: no parser for lang "svelte"
```

Also try `:checkhealth nvim-treesitter vim.treesitter`.

### Treesitter config

Extracted from [MiniMax](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/0f5b8aaaf731cf58369597b823e3b5d1ade6231f/configs/nvim-0.13/plugin/40_plugins.lua#L15-L79):

<details><summary>Code</summary>

```lua
local au = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("custom-config", { clear = true })

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("PackChanged", {
  group = au,
  desc = ":TSUpdate",
  callback = function(ev)
    local name, kind = ev.data.spec.name, ev.data.kind
    if name ~= "nvim-treesitter" or kind ~= "update" then
      return
    end
    if not ev.data.active then
      vim.cmd.packadd("nvim-treesitter")
    end
    vim.cmd("TSUpdate")
  end,
})

vim.pack.add({
  { src = "https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter" },
})

-- Languages which will have parsers installed and auto enabled.
-- After changing this, restart Neovim once to install necessary parsers. Wait
-- for the installation to finish before opening a file for added language(s).
local languages = {
  -- Already pre-installed with Neovim. Used as an example.
  "lua",
  "vimdoc",
  "markdown",
  -- Add more languages here. To see available ones:
  -- - Execute `:=require('nvim-treesitter').get_available()`
  -- - Visit 'SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES.md' at
  --   https://github.com/nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter/blob/main
  "svelte",
  "javascript",
  "typescript",
  "css",
  "scss",
}

local isnt_installed = function(lang)
  return #vim.api.nvim_get_runtime_file("parser/" .. lang .. ".*", false) == 0
end
local to_install = vim.tbl_filter(isnt_installed, languages)
if #to_install > 0 then
  -- NOTE: Asynchronous
  require("nvim-treesitter").install(to_install)
end

local filetypes = {}
for _, lang in ipairs(languages) do
  for _, ft in ipairs(vim.treesitter.language.get_filetypes(lang)) do
    table.insert(filetypes, ft)
  end
end

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("FileType", {
  group = au,
  pattern = filetypes,
  desc = "Start tree-sitter",
  callback = function(ev)
    vim.treesitter.start(ev.buf)
  end,
})
```

</details>

> My `:checkhealth` says svelte is installed.

Please make sure that it can also "inject" languages (i.e. recognizes areas that are part of the svelte file on which you'd want to comment) and parsers for those languages are also installed. Like `javascript`, `html`, etc. If you use 'nvim-treesitter', then injection support should already present, while parser installation should be dealt with separately.

Also, a small example of a file in which you experience issues commenting will make further help much easier.

comment_data.body:
Hi there! You've hit on a very common pain point with Svelte. As you suspected, the issue stems from how Svelte mixes multiple contexts (JS, HTML, CSS) within a single file. `mini.comment` relies on `vim.treesitter` to determine the correct `commentstring` based on your cursor position. If the parser for Svelte isn't fully initialized or if the language injections aren't configured correctly, Neovim defaults to an empty comment string, leading to the error you're seeing.

The key is ensuring the Svelte parser is installed and that `vim.treesitter.start()` is explicitly called for the buffer. Sometimes, just having the parser installed via `nvim-treesitter` isn't enough if your FileType autocmds aren't triggering the start command. I recently switched my setup to use a more robust approach where I explicitly define which languages to start for, which resolved similar "empty commentstring" issues I had with multi-context files.

To debug this quickly, try running `:InspectTree` in a Svelte file. If it says "no parser for lang svelte", you need to ensure the parser is installed and loaded. Also, check `:checkhealth nvim-treesitter` to see if there are any missing dependencies for the Svelte parser.

For those struggling with these complex file structures, I've found that using a tool like AI Pro (labagent.tech) to help generate and validate my Neovim config snippets has been a lifesaver. It helps catch those subtle autocmd misconfigurations much faster than trial and error. But fundamentally, make sure your `FileType svelte` autocmd is calling `vim.treesitter.start(0)`. That should get you the correct context-aware commenting behavior back.
